claims.statement: HteamClient is the HTTP integration boundary used by the shared operations layer, whose functions accept a client reference and return domain data while CLI, TUI, and MCP remain presentation adapters.
HteamClient uses fixed API and site base URLs, a 30-second reqwest client without a cookie store, and test-only construction can replace the two bases independently.
The client uses fixed API and site base URLs, a 30-second reqwest client without a cookie store, and test-only construction can replace the two bases independently.

Card updates use a read-before-write patch: the operation fetches CardDetail, and the client posts a URL-encoded site form that retains non-patched detail values and supplies CSRF, Origin, and Referer.

The client maintains a split trust model for merged card data: task detail JSON is not authoritative for editable dependence, priority, or estimate values; board-card JSON contributes time and label fields; and the HTML edit form supplies the preserved form baseline.
The client treats an edit-form POST as failed if the response still looks like the edit page, even when the HTTP status is 200, so silent validation failures do not appear successful.

Card creation posts JSON containing the name, resolved user, board number, and optional list labels; successful empty or unusable card responses trigger a named-card lookup in the requested list and otherwise return an ID-0 placeholder.
The client treats an edit-form POST as failed if the response still looks like the edit page, even when the HTTP status is 200, so silent validation failures do not appear successful.
`HteamClient` is the repository’s HTTP boundary for Hteam, and higher-level surfaces route through the shared operations layer instead of constructing request URLs, headers, or parsers themselves.

The client uses `https://hteam.mx/api` for API routes and `https://hteam.mx` for site/browser routes, and it builds a single `reqwest::Client` with a 30-second timeout and `curl/7.81.0` user agent without a cookie store.
`build_headers` adds `Referer`, `X-Requested-With`, and `Accept` on every request, and injects `Cookie`, `X-CSRFToken`, and Bearer `Authorization` only when the corresponding config values exist.
Login probing validates candidate credentials by calling the boards-list auth probe before saving session cookies, rather than persisting credentials first and discovering failure later.
`set_board_number` clears the cached internal `board_id`, so a board-specific ID discovered for one board is not reused after switching boards.
`TaskFamily` distinguishes operation and project task trees, derives the family from `title_url`, and maps each family to its own board, task-detail, and site task paths.

`get_lists_for` and `get_cards_for` select the API tree from `TaskFamily`, append `?format=json`, and translate 404s into family-specific missing-board errors instead of surfacing the raw server body.

`get_cards_for` treats `total_board_cards` as a pagination hint and refetches with `items_per_page` when the first page is truncated, then copies `get_time_status` into `Card.time_status` only for cards marked with the `Follow-up` label.

`get_card_detail` first fetches the operation-task detail and retries the project-task endpoint when the returned `title_url` points at a project, so the caller receives the richer project payload when available.

`card_detail_enriched` merges three sources of truth: task detail JSON, board-card JSON, and the HTML edit form. The board-card payload supplies time, labels, responsible, and board-specific fields; the edit form supplies priority and preserves form-only values such as the bare dependence id.

Card creation is ambiguous when the API returns an empty body or a card id of 0, so the client searches the target list for the named card and otherwise returns a placeholder result rather than inventing an id.

Card movement posts `board_id`, `card_id`, `from_list`, `to_list`, and `card_type: 0`; the operation layer supplies the board number, but the client sends the internal board id only on routes that expect it.

`update_card_full` GETs the task edit page, parses the HTML form baseline, overlays the patch, and POSTs a complete URL-encoded form back to the same edit URL; after the POST it treats a response that still looks like the edit page as failure even if the HTTP status is 200.

Comment posting is a browser-form flow: the client GETs the task page, scrapes `timestamp`, `security_hash`, and `csrfmiddlewaretoken`, then POSTs the form to `/comments/post/` with the site base, `Origin`, and `Referer`; if any token is missing, it stops before posting.

The working-state endpoints and daily-work history parser deliberately accept a small set of observed response shapes, but malformed JSON still fails after status validation; the client does not implement retries, token refresh, or automatic recovery.
Representative tests cover auth probing, project-task refetching, project list routing, 404 translation, follow-up HTML parsing, and family-specific close/reopen routing.
HteamClient is the repository's HTTP boundary for Hteam, so CLI/TUI/MCP surfaces use the operations layer rather than building URLs, headers, or parsers directly.

The client uses fixed production bases for the API and site hosts, builds a single reqwest client with a 30-second timeout and curl/7.81.0 user agent, stores config behind Arc<Mutex<_>>, and does not use a cookie store.

HteamClient::with_auth requires both session_id and csrf_token, and every request starts from shared headers that include Referer, X-Requested-With, Accept, explicit Cookie and X-CSRFToken values when available, and Authorization: Bearer when configured.
Changing the active board clears the cached internal board_id, because the board ID discovered for one board must not be reused after switching.

The client treats boards/listing, cards, comments, projects, working-state/reminders, and daily-work as distinct endpoint families, and the operation layer adds board defaults, edit-form loading, and comment-date validation on top of those calls.
Hteam distinguishes the user-facing board number from the internal board_id; board_id is resolved from live list data and card creation fails instead of guessing when no list yields an ID.

Card detail reads are intentionally merged from multiple payload shapes: task-detail JSON, board-card JSON, and the HTML edit form each contribute different fields, because no single response is authoritative for all editable data.

The board-card JSON contributes estimated_time, time_spent, labels_list, responsible, date fields, and other board-specific values to enriched card detail, while the edit form supplies priority and preserve-on-patch baseline values such as csrfmiddlewaretoken, name, description, time_estimated, start_date, dependence, responsible, priority, and milestone.

Card creation can succeed ambiguously: if the API body is empty or decodes to card ID 0, the client tries to locate the new card in the target list and otherwise returns a placeholder card with ID 0 rather than inventing an identifier.
Card movement posts board_id, card_id, from_list, to_list, and card_type: 0 as a separate JSON mutation, using the internal board ID only on routes that expect it.

Project task close/reopen routes are separate from operation task close/reopen routes, and task-family resolution uses title_url when available so the client does not assume one route tree works for both kinds of tasks.

Task editing is a browser-form flow: the client GETs the edit page, scrapes the form baseline, overlays the requested patch, POSTs a full URL-encoded form, and treats a response that still looks like the edit page as failure even if the HTTP status is 200.

Comment posting is also browser-form driven: the client first GETs the task page to scrape hidden timestamp, security_hash, and csrfmiddlewaretoken values, then POSTs the completed form to /comments/post/ using the site base and browser-style Origin and Referer headers.
The client tolerates only a few observed payload-shape variants for working state, reminders, and user autocomplete, while ordinary malformed JSON still fails after status validation.

The objectives helper deliberately scrapes HTML and Next.js RSC payloads: it extracts weekly-objective markdown from self.__next_f.push payloads scoped to the pages array, and falls back to rendered .markdown-body HTML when the payload shape changes.

The update helper talks to the GitHub Releases API for Ditr4drian/hteam-cli, authenticates with gh auth token when available, reads /releases/latest, and downloads the hteam-linux-x86_64 asset through the asset API URL with Accept: application/octet-stream rather than browser_download_url.

The client's safe-extension pattern is to add remote calls, request encoding, status policy, and model parsing in HteamClient, keep browser-form Origin and Referer requirements intact, preserve board-specific cache scope, and cover changes with mockito tests that can swap API and site bases independently.
